sentences.text: Desham Prashanth Kumar D. Prashanth ... vs The State Of
Telangana

on 14 February, 2024
 The Honourable Smt. Justice T. Madhavi Devi

Criminal Petition No.8378 Of 2023
 Order

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) by accused No.4 seeking quashing of the proceedings in C.C.No.5796 of 2018 on the file of the III Metropolitan Magistrate, R.R. District at L.B.Nagar, registered for the offences under Sections 498A, 324, 406, 409, 420, 506, 509, 511 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: III Metropolitan Magistrate, R.R. District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts are that the de facto complainant is the wife of accused No.1, and accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law and accused No.4 is the brother of accused No.1.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that from the averments in the FIR and also the charge sheet, it is clear that no specific allegations have been made against the petitioner herein except for the omnibus allegations of harassment.

He has drawn the attention of this Court to the specific reference to the petitioner herein, wherein the de facto complainant has stated that when she was harassed by her husband in Australia, she had called her brother-in-law, i.e., accused No.4 herein and he and his wife had come and taken her to their home and subsequently she was left with her sister.
The only allegation made against the petitioner herein is that he is staying in Australia illegally and that he has supported his brother.

It is further submitted that except for these allegations, there are no specific allegations against the petitioner vis-a-vis the complainant and the petitioner has been made as an accused only in order to make the other accused yield to the illegal demands of the de facto complainant.
3. Notice has been sent to respondent No.2 which was returned unserved and therefore, substituted service has been taken out and hence it is deemed service.

In spite of the same, there is no representation on behalf of the de facto complainant and therefore, it is presumed that she is not interested in pursuing this petition against the petitioner herein.
4. After going through the contents of the FIR and the charge sheet, it is clear that there is no allegation of any harassment by the petitioner herein from the date of marriage.
Only on one instance, the complainant had requested them to protect her from her husband and accused No.4 and his wife had come to protect her.
The omnibus allegation is that accused Nos.1 to 4 are all harassing her mentally and physically.

Therefore, it will not attract the offences registered under Sections 498A, 324, 406, 409, 420, 506, 509, 511 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act against the petitioner herein.
5. In view of the same, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of proceedings against the petitioner herein is nothing but abuse of process of law.
